request: what's the difference between a percentage point and a percent?

beats.intent: Bars of an interest rate going from 2% to 3%
beats.narration: An interest rate goes up from two percent to three percent.
beats.code:
stage.title("Points or percent?")
b = draw_bars(stage, [2, 3], labels=["before", "after"], color=BLUE)
stage.caption("rate in %")

beats.intent: The gap between the bars marked +1 percentage point
beats.narration: The rate went up by one percentage point: three minus two.
beats.code:
bars = b[0] if len(b) == 2 else b
x0 = bars[0].get_left()[0] - 0.1
level = DashedLine([x0, bars[1].get_top()[1], 0], bars[1].get_corner(UL), color=GREY_B)
gap = Brace(Line([x0, bars[0].get_top()[1], 0], [x0, bars[1].get_top()[1], 0]), LEFT, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(level), GrowFromCenter(gap))
stage.add(level, gap)
stage.label(gap, "+1 point", direction=LEFT, color=YELLOW)

beats.narration: But compared with where it started, it rose by half: a fifty percent increase. Both are true; they answer different questions.

request: how many squares are there on a chessboard?

beats.intent: An 8 by 8 board with one 1×1 square and one 2×2 square outlined
beats.narration: There are sixty four little squares, but also bigger squares made of several: two by two, three by three, up to the whole board.
beats.code:
stage.title("Squares on a chessboard")
board = VGroup(*[Square(0.55, stroke_width=0, fill_color=(GREY_D if (r + c) % 2 else GREY_B), fill_opacity=1)
                 for r in range(8) for c in range(8)]).arrange_in_grid(rows=8, cols=8, buff=0).move_to([-2.5, -0.3, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(board))
stage.add(board)
s1 = Square(0.55, color=RED, stroke_width=5).move_to(board[0])
s2 = Square(1.1, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=5).move_to((board[18].get_center() + board[27].get_center()) / 2)
s3 = Square(1.65, color=GREEN, stroke_width=5).move_to(board[45])
stage.play(Create(s1), Create(s2), Create(s3))
stage.add(s1, s2, s3)

beats.intent: Bars of how many squares of each size: 64, 49, 36, 25, 16, 9, 4, 1
beats.narration: A k by k square can start in 9 minus k places across and down: sixty four of size one, forty nine of size two, down to one of size eight.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
b = draw_bars(stage, [64, 49, 36, 25, 16, 9, 4, 1], labels=["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6", "7", "8"], color=ORANGE)
stage.caption("number of squares of each size")

beats.narration: Add them up: two hundred and four squares.

request: how does a periscope let you see over a wall?

beats.intent: A tall tube with a mirror at 45° at the top and one at the bottom, a wall beside it
beats.narration: A periscope is a tube with two mirrors, each tilted at forty five degrees.
beats.code:
stage.title("A periscope")
tube = Rectangle(width=1.0, height=4.4, color=GREY_B).move_to([0, -0.2, 0])
top_m = Line([-0.5, 1.5, 0], [0.5, 2.5, 0], color=BLUE, stroke_width=8)
bot_m = Line([-0.5, -2.9, 0], [0.5, -1.9, 0], color=BLUE, stroke_width=8)
wall = Rectangle(width=0.6, height=3.0, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.6).move_to([2.2, -1.2, 0])
stage.play(Create(tube), Create(top_m), Create(bot_m), FadeIn(wall))
stage.add(tube, top_m, bot_m, wall)

beats.intent: A light ray coming from the right above the wall, bouncing down at the top mirror and out at the bottom mirror to an eye
beats.narration: Light from beyond the wall hits the top mirror and turns straight down the tube, then the bottom mirror turns it out to your eye.
beats.code:
ray = VMobject(color=YELLOW, stroke_width=5).set_points_as_corners([[5.5, 2.0, 0], [0, 2.0, 0], [0, -2.4, 0], [-3.0, -2.4, 0]])
stage.play(Create(ray), run_time=2)
stage.add(ray)
eye = Ellipse(width=0.6, height=0.35, color=WHITE).move_to([-3.4, -2.4, 0])
stage.play(Create(eye))
stage.add(eye)
stage.label(eye, "eye", direction=DOWN)

beats.intent: The two mirrors each turning the light through 90°
beats.narration: Each mirror turns the light through ninety degrees, so it comes out travelling the way it went in, just lower down.
beats.code:
for p in ([0, 2.0, 0], [0, -2.4, 0]):
    mark = Circle(radius=0.3, color=RED).move_to(p)
    stage.play(Create(mark), run_time=0.4)
    stage.add(mark)
stage.caption("two 90° turns: same direction, lower down")

request: why does a straw look bent in a glass of water?

beats.intent: A glass of water with a straight straw leaning in it
beats.narration: Put a straight straw in a glass of water.
beats.code:
stage.title("The bent straw")
water = Rectangle(width=4, height=2.4, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.25).move_to([0, -1.6, 0])
glass = Rectangle(width=4, height=3.8, color=WHITE).move_to([0, -0.9, 0])
straw = Line([-1.4, -2.6, 0], [1.2, 1.4, 0], color=ORANGE, stroke_width=8)
stage.play(Create(glass), FadeIn(water), Create(straw))
stage.add(glass, water, straw)

beats.intent: A ray from the underwater tip bending away from the vertical at the surface on its way to an eye
beats.narration: Light from the underwater part bends as it leaves the water, away from the vertical, before it reaches your eye.
beats.code:
surf = water.get_top()[1]
tip = np.array([-1.4, -2.6, 0])
exit_p = np.array([-0.1, surf, 0])
ray = VMobject(color=YELLOW, stroke_width=4).set_points_as_corners([tip, exit_p, [2.8, 2.2, 0]])
stage.play(Create(ray))
stage.add(ray)
eye = Ellipse(width=0.5, height=0.3, color=WHITE).move_to([3.0, 2.35, 0])
stage.play(Create(eye))
stage.add(eye)
normal = DashedLine(exit_p + 1.0 * DOWN, exit_p + 1.0 * UP, color=GREY_B)
stage.play(Create(normal))
stage.add(normal)

beats.intent: The eye's straight-back line to where the tip seems to be, higher up: a dashed ghost straw bent at the surface
beats.narration: Your brain assumes light travels straight, so traces it back to a point that is higher than the real tip. The straw seems to bend at the surface.
beats.code:
back = DashedLine(exit_p, exit_p + 1.9 * (exit_p - np.array([2.8, 2.2, 0])) / np.linalg.norm(exit_p - np.array([2.8, 2.2, 0])), color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(back))
stage.add(back)
cross = np.array([-1.4 + 2.6 * (surf + 2.6) / 4.0, surf, 0])
ghost = Line(cross, back.get_end(), color=ORANGE, stroke_opacity=0.5, stroke_width=8)
stage.play(Create(ghost))
stage.add(ghost)
stage.caption("the tip looks higher than it is")
